draft.title: Green water and blue water
card: the moisture held in soil that plants take up through their roots. Rain that soaks into the soil becomes green water.
the water in rivers, lakes, dams and underground stores. People can collect it, pump it or pipe it to where it is needed.
Crops that grow on rain alone, such as dryland wheat, use green water. Crops watered from a dam or a bore use blue water.
Both come from rain. What separates them is where the water is held and how it is used.
draft.remember: Green water is held in soil for plants. Blue water is in rivers, lakes, dams and underground.

a.q: Which of these is an example of blue water?
opts: Water stored in a dam on a river
Moisture in the soil of a paddock
Water taken up by the roots of a gum tree
Rain that has just soaked into a garden bed
a.why: A dam holds water that people can collect and pipe away, so it is blue water. Moisture in the soil of a paddock is tempting, but it is held in soil for plants, which makes it green water.
a.clue: Which one can people collect and send elsewhere?

b.q: Two farms in Tasmania grow potatoes. Ella's crop grows only on rain that soaks into her soil. Sam pumps water from a river to sprinkle his crop. Which statement is correct?
opts: Ella uses green water and Sam uses blue water
Ella uses blue water and Sam uses green water
Both farms use green water, as the water began as rain
Both farms use blue water, as the water began as rain
b.why: Rain held in Ella's soil is green water. Sam collects water from a river, so he uses blue water. Both began as rain, but that does not decide the type. Where the water is held and how it is used does.
b.clue: Ask where the water is held when the plants use it.

a.best: Water stored in a dam on a river

b.best: Ella uses green water and Sam uses blue water

problems.detail: The clue 'Ask where the water is held when the plants use it' can mislead. Sam's sprinkled river water also sits in the soil when his potatoes take it up, so following the clue literally points to 'Both farms use green water'. The clue should ask where the water came from or was held before it reached the crop, such as a river versus the soil.
